name: NY-22
label: Likely D

key_factors: Mannion holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge as the incumbent ($2.7M raised vs. $267K)
Favorable national environment layered on a D+4 district
Kalshi and Polymarket both price the Democratic incumbent near 94%
No public polling and a first-term incumbent leave residual uncertainty
model.rationale: A Democratic-leaning incumbent seat, a strongly favorable environment, and a ten-to-one money advantage over a little-funded challenger point to a comfortable Mannion win; markets pricing near 94 percent and no outside groups investing in the race reinforce that, though the absence of polling keeps the margin anchored to district fundamentals rather than survey data.
model.watch: Any public polling or late outside spending showing Buller gaining traction would narrow the outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Democratic Rep. John Mannion seeks a second term in a Syracuse-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised roughly $2.7 million and holding about $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Kailee Buller has raised about $267,000 with under $200,000 available. Neither side has drawn outside spending so far, and no public polling of the contest is available.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Mannion around 94 percent to win, and no expert raters list the seat as competitive. With a favorable national environment stacked on the district's lean, the fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win, though the lack of surveys leaves room for a closer race than expected. Mannion is the clear favorite heading into November.
